summary: Flavio Geisshuesler works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the universities of Bern, Lausanne, and Virginia (PhD ~2013–2019 under David Germano), holding posts at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (2019, attested 2026) and the University of Sydney (attested 2026).
Flora Blanchon studied under Léon Vandermeersch and Nicole Vandier-Nicolas, and she later taught Jacques Giès.

Florin Deleanu works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bucharest, Peking, Waseda, and Hamburg universities (PhD 1998–2005 under Lambert Schmithausen). He held professorships at Kansai Medical University (1994–2001) and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (2001, 2009).
Florinda De Simini is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She held posts at the University of Naples Federico II (attested 2016) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2017).
Francesca Fremantle specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at SOAS University of London and under Chögyam Trungpa (~1971–1987).

Francesco Sferra is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Raffaele Torella (~1994–1999). He has held positions at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2002), the University of Naples Federico II (attested 2010), and Series Minor (attested 2020).
Francis Brinkley was a scholar in Japanology and linguistics. He studied at the Royal School Dungannon and later held a post at the University of Tokyo (~1878–1881).

Francis Buchanan-Hamilton worked in history and archaeology after receiving his MD at the University of Edinburgh (~1780–1783). He served in the Bengal Medical Service (1794–1815) and directed the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden (1814–1815).

Francis Gladwin was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He was a founding member of the Asiatic Society (~1784–1812) and served as a professor of Persian at Fort William College (~1801–1805).

Francis Harold Cook was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965–1970). He served as a professor at the University of California, Riverside (~1970–1989) and chaired the Numata Center (1999).

Francis N. J. is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He earned a Master's in Ancient History at the University of Calicut, where he also completed doctoral studies under M. R. Raghava Varier (attested 2002).

Francis Robinson is a historian of South Asia and Indology. He completed his PhD at Trinity College, Cambridge (-1970), served as a professor and history department head at Royal Holloway (1990–2004), and was president of the Royal Asiatic Society (1997–2000).

Francis V. Tiso works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Cornell, Harvard, Columbia, and Union Theological Seminary, and has taught Tibetan Buddhism at the Pontifical Gregorian University alongside visiting roles in Rome and San Francisco.
Francis Wilford worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He was a fellow member of the Asiatic Society (~1784–1822) and served as secretary to the committee at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Francis William Bain was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Westminster School and Christ Church, Oxford (~1882–1889), he served as Professor of History and Political Economy at Deccan College (~1892–1919).

Francis Woodman Cleaves was a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Dartmouth and Harvard (PhD ~1933–1942), also studying under Paul Pelliot (1935), and served as a professor at Harvard (1941–1980).

Francis X. Clooney specializes in Indology, religious studies, and comparative theology. After earning his doctorate at the University of Chicago (~1978–1984), he taught at Boston College (1984–2005) and joined Harvard University as Parkman Professor of Divinity in 2005.
Francisco García Ayuso was a scholar in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Munich (~1869–1871) under Martin Haug.

Francisco J. Varela worked in philosophy and cognitive neuroscience. He earned degrees from the University of Chile and Harvard (PhD 1968–1970), holding posts at the University of Chile, CNRS, École Polytechnique, and Pitié-Salpêtrière Hospital.

Franciscus Verellen is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and history. He studied at Hamburg, Oxford, and the EPHE under Kristofer Schipper. He taught at Columbia University (1987–1991) and served as director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1991–2021).
